all_current_assertion_rows.literal_text: S003 fully determines the on-disk contract Slide Scout must read: Zarr v3 groups/arrays described by `zarr.json` files (S003 L68–L72, L87–L100), an `ome`-namespaced metadata block with a hierarchy-consistent `version: "0.5"` (S003 L150–L165), and typed metadata keys (`multiscales`, `axes`, `coordinateTransformations`, `omero`, `labels`/`image-label`, `plate`, `well`, transitional `bioformats2raw.layout` + `series`). The thin plan's core shape — open fileset → list images → canvas with pan/zoom, channel/time/plane controls, label overlays, details panel, responsive background reads, understandable failure messages, read-only local sessions (Viewer.md L5–L11) — is directionally compatible with the source, but the source adds discovery, correctness, navigation, and display obligations the plan does not name: plate/well acquisition-aware discovery, multi-image-collection discovery, arbitrary dataset paths ordered largest→smallest, axis-order and `dimension_names` validation, composed per-level + global scale/translation transforms, unit handling, `omero` channel/window defaults, integer-only same-level-count labels with `image-label` colors, and version/metadata consistency checks. The largest unsupported-input surface comes from S003 L70–L72 ("all features of the Zarr format … may be used … unless explicitly disallowed", with no disallowance found by the recorded whole-capture `disallow`/`codec`/`chunk`/`profile` searches and full-text reads — see N-01): codecs, chunk grids, data types, and storage transformers are unbounded by this source, so the viewer must fail gracefully on whatever its Zarr library cannot decode. Reader-implementation behavior ("Tools", S003 L813–L814) is only a two-line pointer with no further requirements found in the recorded searches (§9, N-02/N-03/N-24), so interoperability with real filesets is asserted by the plan but not evidenced inside S003; the brief's "actual reader implementations" research goal is unresolvable in this scope. All §10 validation is UNEXECUTED.

all_current_assertion_rows.literal_text: - **F-07 — Image open = Zarr group + per-level arrays + chunk decoding (Obligation).** An image is a Zarr group of groups/arrays; group attributes (incl. `multiscales`, `omero`) live in its `zarr.json` (S003 L87–L89). Each pyramid level is a separate Zarr array (folder of chunks) whose own `zarr.json` governs decoding (S003 L91–L100). Chunks decode "conforming to the Zarr array specification" (S003 L99–L100). Zarr v3 parsing is therefore a hard dependency of every plan feature. Plan implication: EXTEND — name the dependency and its failure surface (§7).

all_current_assertion_rows.literal_text: - **F-08 — Three fileset shapes; sniff in precedence order (Obligation).** S003 defines three top-level shapes the opener must distinguish: (1) single/multi-image plain layout (`123.zarr`, `456.zarr` image groups, S003 L82–L100); (2) HCS plate layout `plate → row → well → field-of-view images` (S003 L118–L148 plus §2.7–§2.8); (3) transitional `bioformats2raw` collection (`series.ome.zarr` with `bioformats2raw.layout`, `OME/` group, numbered image groups, S003 L175–L275). The thin plan says only "opens a local OME-Zarr 0.5 fileset and lists the images it finds" (Viewer.md L5) — the recorded plan search for `plate`/`collection`/`series`/`multiscales` finds none of these shapes named (N-05). Disposition: EXTEND (required). The opener must sniff, in order: `plate` (takes precedence where present, S003 L204–L206, L262), else `bioformats2raw.layout`, else `multiscales` (single image), and report shape ambiguity rather than guessing (§3.2–§3.3).

all_current_assertion_rows.literal_text: - **F-11 — HCS plate discovery (Obligation).** Plate group implements `plate` (S003 L125–L127); wells enumerated by `plate.wells[].path = "<row>/<column>"` with 0-based `rowIndex`/`columnIndex` all referring to the same pair (S003 L552–L560); each well lists fields of view in `well.images[].path` (+ `acquisition` when multiple acquisitions exist, S003 L744–L750). Empty row/well groups SHOULD NOT be present (S003 L128–L129). Plan's flat "lists the images it finds" cannot express plate → well → field/acquisition identity. Disposition: EXTEND (required); listing chrome (tree vs flat with well/acquisition qualifiers) is a product decision, the underlying enumeration is obligatory.

The value `3` is unexplained anywhere in the recorded searches (N-07): accept only `3`, reject/flag anything else. Plan is silent. Disposition: EXTEND (required).

Each `datasets[]` entry MUST contain `path` (relative to the image group) and `coordinateTransformations` (S003 L305–L308). `datasets[].path`s MUST be ordered from largest (highest resolution) to smallest (S003 L305–L306; recorded `MUST be ordered from largest` / `largest` / `smallest` searches confirm this is the sole ordering sentence). all_current_assertion_rows.literal_text: - **F-25 — Rank, composition, order, names (Obligation).** `axes` length 2–5, equal to array rank (S003 L173, L299–L300); MUST contain 2–3 `type: space` entries, MAY add one `type: time` and one `type: channel` **or** null/custom type (S003 L301; recorded `null` search confirms this is the sole null-type sentence). Image arrays "must be up to 5-dimensional with the axis of type time before type channel, before spatial axes" (S003 L96–L97). Entries MUST parallel array dimension order AND MUST be type-ordered time → channel/custom → space (S003 L302). Three spatial axes with planar `yx` + stacking `z` SHOULD order `zyx` (S003 L303). Every `axes[].name` MUST be unique (S003 L168); `dimension_names` MUST match (S003 L174). Axis names are arbitrary (S003 L81); 2-D (yx), 3-D, 4-D, and 5-D images are all conforming. The viewer MUST derive its t/c/z sliders from `axes` order + `type`, never from assumed `tczyx` positions: hide the t-slider when no `time` axis exists, hide channel controls when no `channel`/custom axis exists, and treat "plane" as the two innermost spatial axes per `axes`. The plan's "time-point and plane selection where relevant" (Viewer.md L5) is correct in spirit but must be axis-driven. Disposition: EXTEND.

all_current_assertion_rows.literal_text: - **F-27 — `omero` MUST-fields vs example-only siblings (Obligation + scoped absence).** Channel identity comes from `axes`; rendering defaults (transitionally) from `omero`. The `omero` block is "optional, but if present it MUST contain … `channels`" (S003 L426). Each entry MUST contain `color` (6 hex RGB digits, S003 L427) and `window` with `min`/`max`/`start`/`end` (S003 L428–L430; recorded `window`/`color` searches confirm these are the sole normative sentences). Obligations when `omero` is present: apply `window.start/end` as the initial contrast limits within `min/max`, and `color` as the initial channel color. Honor `active`/`label`/`rdefs.defaultT/defaultZ/model` as best-effort initial state (initial visibility ← `active`, initial t/z ← `defaultT`/`defaultZ`, initial compositing ← `model`), but never require them. (c) Absent `omero`, no embedded defaults were found in scope (N-16): all rendering state (visibility, color, contrast, initial t/z) is a product decision (sensible defaults + session-local persistence, Viewer.md L9); the details panel should state "no embedded display defaults" in that case. all_current_assertion_rows.literal_text: - **F-29 — Transform vocabulary + per-level + global composition (Obligation).** `coordinateTransformations` is an ordered list applied sequentially (S003 L279–L293): `identity` (default, usually implicit, S003 L282–L283); `translation` (`translation: float[]` or binary `path`, S003 L284–L286); `scale` (`scale: float[]` or binary `path`, S003 L287–L289; recorded `binary` search confirms these are the sole binary-path sentences). Each `datasets[]` entry's list MUST contain only `translation`/`scale` (S003 L308–L309); MUST contain exactly one scale expressing "pixel size in physical units or time duration", or — where scaling is unavailable/inapplicable for an axis — "the scaling factor between the current resolution and the first resolution for the given axis, defaulting to 1.0 if there is no downsampling along the axis" (S003 L310); MAY contain exactly one translation = offset from origin in physical units, which MUST follow scale so it is expressed in physical coordinates (S003 L311); scale/translation vectors MUST match `axes` length (S003 L312). `multiscales[].coordinateTransformations` MAY exist, follows the same type/order rules, and is "applied … after" the per-level transforms (S003 L314–L315; recorded `applied after` search confirms the sole composition sentence) — e.g. a shared time scale (example S003 L368–L374 scales `t` by 0.1 ms uniformly, L320–L387). Physical coordinate = `global(scale∘translate) ∘ perLevel(scale∘translate)` applied to integer data indices, in listed order (S003 L293, L314–L316). The viewer MUST compose both levels; applying only per-level transforms miscalibrates every axis the global transform touches. No worked multi-axis global example beyond time was found in scope (N-25); the outer∘inner reading is the only composition consistent with "applied after".

all_current_assertion_rows.literal_text: - **F-30 — Worked calibration + details-panel content (Derived requirements).** Normative example (S003 L320–L387): 5-D `tczyx`, t-unit ms, xyz-unit µm; level 0 scale `[1,1,0.5,0.5,0.5]`, level 1 `[1,1,1,1,1]`, level 2 `[1,1,2,2,2]`; global `[0.1,1,1,1,1]`. Physical voxel at level 0: Δt = 0.1 ms, Δc dimensionless ×1, Δxyz = 0.5 µm. The details panel must show per-axis `name / type / unit / per-level scale / global scale / composed physical extent`, and the cursor readout must convert hover indices through the composed transform of the currently displayed level. Required content: dimensions (rank + per-axis array extents per level + `axes[].name`), units (per-axis `unit` or "none/unknown"), coordinates (composed physical position of cursor / view center + voxel size at current level), plus pyramid identity (`multiscales[].name/type`, level path, downscaling note). The plan names "dimensions, units and coordinates" but not the two-level composition, per-level voxel sizes, or unit caveats. Disposition: EXTEND (required for "correctly calibrated").

all_current_assertion_rows.literal_text: - **F-31 — Calibration edge cases (Ambiguities + Unsupported input).** (a) Scale-fallback reading (S003 L310): for axes without physical scaling the value is a relative factor vs level 0 (default 1.0). The viewer cannot know from the number alone whether a `1.0` is "1 physical unit" or "no downsampling" — it MUST pair every scale with its axis's `unit` presence: no `unit` ⇒ report "uncalibrated (relative scale N)" rather than inventing units. Channel axes never have meaningful physical scale; display channel index, not converted coordinates. (b) "Offset from the origin" (S003 L311) never defines the origin — the recorded `origin` search finds only the L311 sentence plus unrelated `original` substrings (N-17); treat translations as relative to the image-group frame and say so. (c) Binary-`path` scale/translation (S003 L285–L289) has no dtype/shape/endianness rule in the recorded `dtype`/`endian`/`shape` searches (all no-hit) or the `binary` read (N-18): unsupported input unless the Zarr backend resolves it; the message must name the transform and level. (d) Missing scale transform, wrong vector length, non-scale/translation types in image transforms, or translation-before-scale all violate S003 L309–L312: malformed-level handling (§3.5), never silent reinterpretation.

all_current_assertion_rows.literal_text: - **F-34 — Alignment: same-coordinate-system with a documented gap (Near-obligation).** Labels are "in the same coordinate system … (usually having the same dimensions and coordinate transformations)" (S003 L432–L433; recorded `usually` search confirms this and the transitional L62 occurrence only); the layout overview adds "each dimension … either the same as the corresponding dimension … or 1 if … irrelevant" (S003 L106–L108). "Usually" + overview-only broadcast rule = uncertain normative force (N-26). Implement: render the label level corresponding to the current image level (same index, counts being equal), broadcast length-1 label axes, verify composed transforms match where present, and warn visibly on any mismatch (different extents beyond broadcastable 1s, different scales) rather than silently stretching. Whether a label image's own `axes`/`coordinateTransformations` or the parent's govern alignment when both exist is unstated in the recorded searches (N-20); implement "label's own transforms, verified against parent's, warn on divergence" and record the assumption. Never resample labels with interpolating filters as if they were intensity data — values are categorical (`0`/`1` cellular example, S003 L434–L435, L513–L514); the recorded `interpolat`/`nearest`/`resampl` searches find no source resampling rule (N-21), so nearest-neighbor overlay rendering is nearest-neighbor by semantic necessity recorded as a product decision justified by the integer-label contract.

Viewer rules: honor `rgba` incl. alpha compositing; entries without `rgba` need a deterministic fallback palette (product decision, documented); surface `properties` in the details panel / legend; follow `source.image` only to annotate provenance (default `"../../"`), not to relocate the overlay.

This is a scope limitation, not a finding of incompatibility. The limit of the negative: keyword misses prove only those searches; a paraphrased implementation sentence using none of the searched terms would not have been caught — but the full L813–L820 read (Implementations + Citing) independently confirms no requirements text there.

exact_original_criterion.half: Mentions version validation or metadata layout, but does not connect the two to admission.
exact_original_criterion.missed: Assumes legacy metadata is 0.5-compatible, silently mixes versions, or offers only generic error handling.

E01.title: Recommended label keys presented as mandatory presence
E01.finding: The image-label object SHOULD contain colors/version. Value types and label-value keys are MUST constraints when supplied. Both current reports promote recommended key presence to MUST; this changes admission/validation conditions.

E02.title: Coordinate-frame requirement weakened by qualifier inference
E02.finding: R019 quotes the coordinate-system sentence accurately but uses usually/overview-only wording to weaken its force; R018 summarizes usually same system. Source usually qualifies dimensions/transforms, not the coordinate-system identity. Full conformance context and supported-overlay association conditions remain governing.

E03.title: Relative source identity reduced to provenance
E03.finding: R019 directs source.image to annotate provenance only, not relocate the overlay. An explicit relative original-image reference identifies which image the label derives from; supported overlays must resolve that association before registration. R018 mentions the worked source example but does not supply a complete standalone relative-source/two-origin admission rule.
E03.outcome: R019 contradicted/unsafe narrowing; R018 partial/unresolved association

E04.title: Scale/translation expression conflicts with listed-order prose
E04.finding: R019 writes global(scale∘translate) ∘ perLevel(scale∘translate). Under standard composition notation that applies translation before scale, contrary to its correct listed-order prose. Correct transform per stage is translation after scale; group after dataset. Both reports use a scale-only example that cannot detect reversed/omitted offsets.
E04.outcome: R019 internally inconsistent; original concrete offset check absent in both

E05.title: Color/window semantics exceed mere field presence
E05.finding: Source constrains RGB encoding and gives minimum/maximum/start/end value meanings. R018 Clarification C and R019 N-15 broadly limit normative semantics to field presence. Lack of a gamma registry or extra range/clamping policy can remain qualified, but it does not erase the positive constraints.
E05.outcome: contradicted broad assertion; narrower absences qualified

E06.title: Informative example called normative
E06.finding: R019 F-30 calls the worked scale example normative although examples are informative. Numeric scale arithmetic is correct. R018 explicitly corrects this terminology. Descriptive assertions outside informative sections can be normative without uppercase RFC tokens; missing keywords alone do not settle force.
E06.outcome: R019 contradicted terminology; R018 correction supported

E07.title: Generic feature permission does not erase positive label constraints
E07.finding: R018 explicitly reports no dtype disallowance observed; R019 records broader no-Zarr-feature-disallowance headline with search limits. Retain the qualified generic-permission risk, but integer-only label dtype constraints remain positive conditions. Neither absence wording proves all features/dtypes valid in every role or whole-original source absence.
E07.outcome: qualified; no blanket global absence credit

E08.title: Claimed review/session/seed events remain historical assertions
E08.finding: Sequential reads, all seed units preserved/verified, claimed tool inventory/no execution, all obligations intact, native completion and usage totals require their own admitted source/native proof. Stage1 contains current claims about those events, not the original session or full seed. No acquisition or novelty credit follows from self-report.

E09.title: Original decoding/fill authority is not positively mapped
E09.finding: The exact Zarr core/bytes/transpose/filesystem source URIs in original C07/C08 have no catalog alias in the current profile. S055 shows actual sharding/little-endian codec/fill metadata, not those full normative bodies. Missing positive authority/predecessor locators are unresolved; no substitute is fetched and no candidate acquisition failure is inferred.

E10.title: Original precision/codec/fill adversarial obligations absent
E10.finding: Current test/proposal coverage lacks sparse/scrambled uint64 identity above binary64 exact range, asymmetric transpose plus big-endian decoding/unsupported combinations, and absent nonzero-fill versus unreadable existing/malformed/cancel states. These original facets remain assigned; generic unsupported-data/read-only prose does not constitute full coverage.

E11.title: Actual reader source needs version/capability/error boundaries
E11.finding: Admitted static reader captures contain substantive interoperability leads beyond S003. S018 follows relative label source, keys metadata by integers, takes first multiscale and constructs zero tiles on some ValueError paths. S019 separates explicit read mode from writable construction, documents None for missing/error and delegates chunks to dask. S048 includes first dataset transform selection, parent-transform inheritance, label group traversal and parent opens with unresolved dependency defaults. These are static, separately pinned captures, not proof of an installed release or candidate execution. Whole original reader investigation remains partial.
